selectTopicKNN materialized every above-threshold candidate per member
and fully sorted the list before cutting to k.

Base measured: main tip 267681cefd0622800e56033d2d2e80c7278d20db.
Command (both legs identical):

    cd cmd/knowledge && go test ./internal/thought/ -run 'TestSelectTopicKNN_' -v

The cost gate calls selectTopicKNN once over an all-pairs-admitted topic (every
pair clears the threshold, which is the regime the ticket names) at k=4, and
measures allocated bytes per call. Doubling the membership doubles the pairs
SELECTED and quadruples the pairs COMPARED, so the materializing shape predicts a
ratio near 4 and a bounded one near 1.


=== RED — against the per-member full sort (densify.go:88) ===

selectTopicKNN allocation: 600 members -> 19974032 B/call (1965 pairs);
                          1200 members -> 121238114 B/call (2560 pairs)

    --- FAIL: TestSelectTopicKNN_AllocationScalesWithSelectedPairsNotComparedPairs
        --- PASS: .../instrument_is_live
        --- FAIL: .../allocation_does_not_scale_with_compared_pairs
              "121238114" is not less than "59922096"
              doubling the membership took allocation from 19974032 B to
              121238114 B per call — the selection is materializing every
              compared candidate, not just the ones it keeps
        --- FAIL: .../allocation_is_bounded_by_the_selected_pairs
              "121238114" is not less than "1966080"
              selecting 2560 pairs must cost under 1966080 B, not 121238114 B

Observed ratio 121238114/19974032 = 6.07 — above the quadratic prediction of 4
because the candidate slice's growth doubling reallocates on the way up.

The instrument_is_live control PASSED in the red run.

TestSelectTopicKNN_TieBreakIsUnchanged PASSED in the red run: that is how its
golden was captured, against the pre-swap sort-then-cut implementation.


=== GREEN — after offering candidates to searchengine.HitHeap ===

selectTopicKNN allocation: 600 members -> 711504 B/call (1965 pairs);
                          1200 members -> 842836 B/call (2560 pairs)

    --- PASS: TestSelectTopicKNN_AllocationScalesWithSelectedPairsNotComparedPairs
    --- PASS: TestSelectTopicKNN_TieBreakIsUnchanged

Reduction: 121238114 -> 842836 B/call at 1200 members (143.8x), 19974032 ->
711504 at 600 members (28.1x). Ratio 6.07 -> 1.18, i.e. allocation now tracks the
pairs selected rather than the pairs compared.


=== TIE-BREAK EQUIVALENCE — why the swap preserves the selection ===

The old selection sorted each member's candidates by (score descending, partner ID
ascending) and cut to k. HitHeap.Offer instead replaces the worst kept hit only on
a STRICT score improvement, so a newcomer that TIES the worst kept hit is rejected
and the incumbent — the EARLIER-OFFERED one — survives. That is arrival-order
tie-breaking, not ID tie-breaking.

The two coincide because selectTopicKNN sorts its members and builds each
candidate list by ranging that sorted slice, so candidates arrive in ascending ID
order. Rejection is monotone in arrival order at a fixed score: the heap's root
score never falls, so if a smaller-ID candidate at score s was rejected, every
later tie at s is rejected too. The kept tied subset is therefore a prefix of the
tied candidates in ID order — exactly what the sort-then-cut kept. The member sort
is consequently load-bearing for the tie-break and not merely for output
determinism, which is what the docstring now records.

MUTATION CHECK ON THE GOLDEN. HitHeap.Offer's `>` was temporarily changed to `>=`
(last-offered wins a tie). TestSelectTopicKNN_TieBreakIsUnchanged went RED and the
diff showed the p1-partnered pairs replaced by p5-partnered ones — the tie-break
inverted, exactly the property the golden exists to pin. The mutant was reverted.
